newsitem.title: UK: RUSSIAN DEBT FIRM IN MIXED BRADY BOND MARKET.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN DEBT FIRM IN MIXED BRADY BOND MARKET.

text.p: Russian loans continued last week's bull run on Monday in a thin and edgy Brady bond market looking for direction from U.S. Treasuries and key U.S. data due this week.
Dealers said Russia was the only real feature as investors, including buyers out of Asia, continued to pick up paper on the belief that a London Club debt restructuring deal was now assured.

Moscow said on Friday it had fully reconciled 70 percent of the $24 billion principal of the $35 billion total commercial debt, which was taken on by Vneshekonombank after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
Dollar-denominated Vnesh loans RUVNUSLNS=RR added 3/8 to 100-7/8 bid while PRINs RUPRIN=RR traded as high as 73-1/2 before slipping back on profit-taking to stand 1/8 higher at 72-3/4 bid.
Other Brady debt was mixed as investors remained glued to U.S. long bond prices, which were recovering in Europe after Friday's sharp fall.
"There's nothing new on the emerging market fundamentals, so everyone is nervously watching the long bond," said one dealer.
Attention is now focused on Wednesday's U.S. producer price and retail sales reports to determine direction in U.S. Treasuries.
A Reuter survey of economists expected overall and core producer prices to each gain 0.1 percent. July retail sales were seen up 0.7 percent and up 0.5 percent without autos.

"We are waiting for U.S. data. But the Brady market is still positive as a whole," said a second dealer."Spreads have hardy moved. We've actually tightened on some assets. People still want to buy the market with a (U.S. 30-year Treasury) yield of 6.62 percent."
Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR were up 1/4 at 95-1/2, as were Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR at 83-1/8. But Mexico Pars MX625L19=RR shed 1/8 to 80-1/4 and Bulgaria FRBs BGFLIRB=RR lost 1/4 at 62-1/2.
